exact_statement: Using a many-primes-in-one-dyadic-interval input, prove that for every prime b and fixed integer A>=4, all sufficiently large N=b^K contain a support-minimal unequal-cardinality equal-product path wholly in (N/b^6,N] that avoids every prescribed prime below b^(floor(K/2)-A). Deduce deterministic and shared-seed randomized adaptive valuation-query lower bounds for zero transcripts reaching to within a fixed factor of sqrt(N), with an exact density-sensitive success-probability inequality. Establish the square-root limitation of this path host. Do not claim global alteration bounds, a full transversal estimate, or resolution of Erdos 786.
scope_notes: Variant lock: the relation uses disjoint Finsets of distinct integers with equal products and unequal cardinalities; support minimality is required.

The predecessor Q.1--Q.4 campaign is frozen at independent_audit and is read-only. This campaign must improve the observation cutoff from N^(1/2-epsilon) to a fixed multiplicative distance below sqrt(N).

The only new analytic dependency permitted is the standard consequence of the prime number theorem that (X,2X) contains asymptotic order X/log X primes. It is used solely to supply 2 floor(K/4) distinct edge labels when X grows exponentially in K.
The decision-tree model remains one uniform finite exact-valuation tree per K and shared random seed, with a terminating all-zero branch. Off-zero branches are unrestricted.
The randomized result must retain the exact finite bound Pr(transversal)<=E|D|/(L-t), not just an asymptotic slogan.
The square-root boundary is a statement about this path-incidence host: two incident edge primes both greater than sqrt(N) force their rough product above N.
No lower or upper bound on the complete tau(H_N), no global repair lower bound, and no solution of Erdos 786 may be inferred.
Public search for an exact solution remains prohibited; ordinary prime-distribution background may be source-grounded later.
